_: English release notes of QTRIG — automatically loaded instead of co-je-noveho.json when the app runs in English. Same structure (v, datum, nadpis, body); v must match SHELL_CACHE.

verze.nadpis: Sun, Moon and planets behind the globe, sky moves smoothly
body: Space behind the globe moves smoothly. Stars and constellations used to redraw only after a pan ended (they jumped); now they follow the globe frame by frame (precomputed star catalogue, a frame costs a few ms).

Sun, Moon and five planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) at their real places in the sky for today’s date and hour: the Moon with the correct phase and its lit side facing the Sun, the Sun with a corona, Saturn with rings. A body that would fall outside the narrow screen is pulled to the edge in the direction where it really is — like “target off the strip” in AR.
Wider field of view around the globe. Still decoration only — nothing is measured from it.

verze.nadpis: Constellations behind the globe, north by Polaris, a card on astronomical orientation
body: Constellations behind the globe (3D view). Stars and 17 constellations (Ursa Major, Cassiopeia, Orion, Crux, Scorpius…) lie on the real celestial sphere: the sky behind the Earth matches today’s sidereal time and the place you look at, it moves with the globe and turns with it. The Milky Way follows the real galactic plane. Just for pleasure — nothing is measured from it.

Compass check by Polaris. The night sibling of the check by the Sun (Compass → Check by Polaris): aim the rear camera at Polaris and the app tells the compass deviation. Polaris is within 1° of true north and the app computes the rest from time and position — no magnetometer, no signal, no declination. It also shows the height of Polaris above the horizon (= your latitude) and how to find it from the Big Dipper.
Geo card “Polaris = true north” in Learn: why the stars are the oldest geodetic network (azimuth, latitude, longitude, Laplace points).

verze.nadpis: Space behind the globe in the 3D view
body: When you zoom the 3D view out into a globe, space lies behind it: stars, the band of the Milky Way and the Moon in its real phase for today (waxing = right side lit, as seen from Europe), a blue rim of atmosphere around the Earth and sunlight from the top left — the same direction that lights the terrain. Rotate the globe with two fingers and the stars turn with it.

The sky is drawn once and nothing in it animates, so it costs no battery. It hides when you zoom back into the flat map; in the tilted view the sky above the horizon now has the theme colour instead of a bare background.

verze.nadpis: Third round: start without signal without “Something went wrong”, hints lead where things are, connection state from real data
body: Starting without signal no longer reports “Something went wrong”. The vector map is the default and when its data cannot be downloaded (no signal) it is a network state, not an app error — no toast on the sign-in screen; the Map row in Settings says it will retry once the signal returns.

Hints lead where things really are. Eleven messages pointed to the “More” menu hidden since August: the bin is Tools → Record → Restore a deleted point, the error log Tools → Other tools, saving for offline Settings → Job and data, Write to the author is the strip at the top of Tools. The “Other tools” tab in Tools is now named that way (it used to translate as “Next”). The gate’s “More options” explains how the workspace from registration relates to a company.

Connection state from whether data really flows. The GPS detail no longer claims “Internet is up” just because the phone has a network: it is computed from the last real reply (ČÚZK, cloud, map data). On one bar it reports Weak signal with the time of the last reply; the “Downloading data…” pill says after 15 s without a reply that ČÚZK points did not arrive and it keeps trying.

Visual: the toolbar in Sketch / Tacheometry wraps into two rows on a phone (From points, Undo, basemap and export visible at once); dock labels no longer break words with large text; the four actions in the card of an official point sit in a 2×2 grid, equal height.

Languages: four Czech texts remained in the English New point dialog (quality code, Why?, terrain height) — translated. French: 169 live texts with numbers (GPS pill, point counts, months, directions…) were Italian by mistake — now French.

For development: the CI regression tests had been red since v368 (three checks assumed five languages) — fixed; the last regression state is shown in the owner console and in the release-check summary; a new check makes sure no message points to the removed menu.

verze.nadpis: Walk-through: Settings links after the rebuild, French texts with numbers, decimal commas
body: French: texts with a number inside (the “GPS no fix 8 s · position uncertain” pill, “5 min ago”, months in the Yearbook, weather, bin…) were shown in Italian in the French app — 168 patterns are now really French and the data check guards against a repeat.

Links into Settings after the rebuild (v365): “Show filters” for hidden point types, “Max. points in AR”, the Change button next to Measurement country in the Map panel and Settings next to Accuracy from the map led to a different page than where the option lives. The You are measuring in card, messages and guides now give the right paths (Map and points, Backup and maintenance, Tools → Is everything working?) and the basemap is called Map, not Vector.
The “You are measuring in” card shows the coordinates of that country (Poland = PL-2000, not S-JTSK); “What the app can do here” is a proper button.

Tools: the Point sketch on the map tile was missing (search and the task list led nowhere); Parcel has one minimise button instead of two; Underground networks — the coordinate switches sit on one line; Acoustic rangefinder — the sound option fits a narrow screen.

Numbers with a decimal comma in Czech: Maintenance “Used 0,0 MB of ~3,0 GB”, Is everything working? (“±3,0 m”), Sun and light (shadow), Safety in the field (S-JTSK 741 789,46), Inside a building, Poster of the day; the Day log uses the right plural for a single point.

verze.nadpis: “You are measuring in” card: right after the start abroad, not only after crossing a border
body: Whoever downloads the app abroad learns it right away. After starting in a country other than Czechia (once per country) the card You are measuring in: … pops up — the coordinate system and heights of that country, whether the state publishes official points here (yes: Czechia, Slovakia, Switzerland, Netherlands — the app downloads them; no: the map shows only your own points), whether there is a cadastre and which orthophoto. Before, the country was announced only after crossing a border, with two messages in a row — now it is one card, also when crossing.

The card waits until the app is running and nothing covers it (gate, first-measurement guide, another dialog). You can open it again any time in Settings → Map and points → Measurement country → What the app can do here; under the country picker there is a line saying where geodetic control is public.
The foreign-country simulation reports with a toast, not a dialog (it overrode the card), and no longer claims that “there are no ČÚZK points here” — in Switzerland and the Netherlands there are.

verze.nadpis: Official points in Switzerland and the Netherlands; the app says where the state publishes points
body: Official points in Switzerland and the Netherlands. Where the state provides geodetic control as open data, the app downloads it around you by itself — besides Czechia (ČÚZK) and Slovakia (GKÚ SR) now Switzerland (swisstopo: Lagefixpunkte LFP1/LFP2, Höhenfixpunkte HFP1/HFP2 with LN02 height, point protocol as PDF) and the Netherlands (Kadaster RDinfo: Rijksdriehoek points with a photo of the point). On the map, in AR and in guidance they behave like the Czech ones; the point card has a Source row.

Where there are no points, the app says so. Poland, Austria, Germany, France and other states do not publish geodetic control (their geoportals require a key or payment) — after crossing a border the message says directly “The state does not publish official points here — the map shows only your own points” and the Points panel lists the four countries where it is public. So people abroad do not expect points to appear.

Honestly: in those countries surveying today is done with a rover using corrections from the national network (SAPOS, APOS, ASG-EUPOS…) and the surveyor sets up their own points — the app works there with your own points, the drawing and the calibrations.

verze.nadpis: The app speaks French, own map for all of Europe, weather by country
body: French. The sixth language after English, German, Polish, Spanish and Italian — the core and the whole extension (6,600 texts), the “?” guides of the tools, Regulations, Exercises, Geo cards and this changelog (all 120 releases). A phone set to French picks it by itself; otherwise Settings → Appearance.

Own vector map for all of Europe. Map data (buildings, roads, water, rails, forest) are uploaded country by country to the GitHub release “mapa-data” — today already Slovakia, Austria, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, the Baltics, the Balkans and the small states; large countries (Germany, France, Poland, Italy, Spain…) are being added in parts, because one file may be at most 2 GB. The app picks the right part by your position itself (data/mapa-dily.json), nothing to set up. Where data are not there yet, the raster keeps running.

Weather by country. Regional models (ČHMÚ ALADIN, GeoSphere AROME, Météo-France AROME, KNMI HARMONIE, MET Norway, ItaliaMeteo, UK Met Office, MeteoSwiss) are called only in the country they compute for — before, AROME France was asked even for Prague and returned numbers from the edge of its grid. Global models and ensembles run everywhere, so the forecast outside Czechia also comes from 20+ sources.

Honestly: official points (geodetic control) are publicly available as data only in Czechia and Slovakia — elsewhere the states do not publish them (Poland, Austria, Germany have only map services or sell them). Cadastre via map is in SK, PL, AT, NL, FR, CH, SI, BE, HU; orthophoto everywhere (national where it exists, Esri elsewhere).

verze.nadpis: Monthly check: no spurious alerts, empty hub, English without Czech leftovers
body: No toasts when offline: an unloaded map tile, font glyph or terrain tile in the 3D view no longer shows “Something went wrong” for every address — they are only written to the error log.
The “Align differently” hub is no longer built: since v360 all its members are hidden, and via search it opened an empty window with just Close.

English and other languages: hub subtitles in Tools (Fix GPS, Two phones, Conditions) are translated tool by tool; 70 keys and patterns added (the “GPS without a fix N s” pill, Where you can measure, New point without an elevation model, the point card, Point hunters, Formulas, Sun shadow…); the note field of a point has a translated hint.
Light theme: the “Map” card thumbnail in Base map is no longer a white square.
Epochs / monitoring: the window’s close cross overlapped the Close pill in the header.

Texts: the guide and the “What to take” checklist no longer refer to the removed “What you do today” strip; sign-up says the password can be reset with the recovery code (previously “the password cannot be recovered”).

verze.nadpis: The “Who are you?” question removed
body: The Student / Surveyor / Company question after the first launch is gone (together with the profiles from the previous release). The app behaves the same for everyone; the “Learn” group in Tools stays, just not at the top.

verze.nadpis: Settings rebuilt: what matters first, the rest aside
body: Settings has been rebuilt. When you open it you see the Frequent card — point range in the camera and on the map, the cap on AR points, light/dark, outdoor mode and the types of official points — and below it eight categories as rows: AR camera, Map and points, Appearance, Controls, Performance and battery, Job and data; “Less often” at the bottom with backup and account. Every row has a subtitle with its contents, and a page has Back at the top.
Tabs, the side index, “Short settings” and collapsible sections are gone — the layout itself keeps the structure. Inside a page there is only one collapsed “Advanced”.

Profiles (the Field/Precision/Demo settings profile, the work profile and the “What are you doing today” strip in Tools) are removed. Only the device profile (phone calibration) remains under Backup and maintenance.
Duplicates left Settings: Write to the author and Is everything working? are in Tools; Where I work, Pro version, Switch user and Company administration have rows on the Account and app page.

verze.nadpis: The route no longer swims across a pond or a river
body: The route to a point no longer runs straight across water: when a pond or a river blocks the way and the bridge or dam is further than the app looked (40 m around), it looks up to 250 m and then 800 m and finds a way around. It still crosses a brook or a ditch — small water is fine. If there is no crossing within 800 m, it stops at the water and shows the rest dashed as before.

verze.nadpis: Geo newsletter switched off
body: The Geo newsletter is gone from the app (the item in the More menu, the daily issue and the line in the "Today in the field" briefing). Nothing is deleted — the code, data and daily build stay in the repository in case it comes back.

verze.nadpis: Route from a building without the "Exit" ring
body: When you're standing inside a building, the route to the point is still computed via the exit, but the ring with the label "Exit (estimate: street side)" no longer shows in the map — only the dashed stretch to the exit remains.

verze.nadpis: Everything translated: release notes and Update history in five languages, Newsletter per language
body: What's new and Update history are in English, German, Polish, Spanish and Italian — all 118 releases since the first version (data/co-je-noveho-xx.json, 559 texts). Days in the history are spelled out in the app's language (Friday 18 September 2026), counts of days and changes and release numbers go through patterns.

The Geo newsletter reads the issue per language (data/zpravodaj-xx.json): rubrics, the editorial, "Read the original at the source" and the footer are in the dictionary, today's issue is translated by hand. The daily build (scripts/build-zpravodaj.mjs) can translate the issue itself when the repository has the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY key — without it the articles stay in their original language and stale translations are deleted so the foreign-language app doesn't show yesterday's news.

The foreign-language app keeps the release notes and the newsletter on the phone (DICT_CACHE, refreshed in the background; the ?t= stamp no longer fills the cache with copies) and downloads them again after switching language.
Test test_jazyky_data extended to 113 checks (release notes: same structure, HTML and v/date in all languages; newsletter; History and Newsletter in the browser in Italian without a Czech sentence).

verze.nadpis: Navigation even to a distant point, base map Map · Orthophoto · Cadastre, Tools reviewed and tidied, Settings → Application
body: The terrain route to a point now also leads to a levelling or trigonometric point kilometres away: up to 3 km in detail as before, up to 20 km along roads and tracks from a coarser map (over 20 km a straight line). A target on a building wall (levelling bolt) — the route goes right up to it, not just "to the nearest spot".

The map base is two tabs: Map (own vector map, now on from the start — when there's no data or the phone is weaker, a raster quietly runs underneath) and Orthophoto; next to them Cadastre as a parcel switch over the base. The plain raster map as an option is gone.

Tools reviewed one by one: set aside (not deleted — find them by search) went the tape in the camera, check distances, volumes, route track, quality report, point verification, the "don't know where to start" guide, the Align differently signpost, visual stabilisation, surroundings tour, offline vector map, signal prediction and today in the field. Align AR = Compass and Align north.

Precise measurement has six rows instead of nine: Fix GPS (walking along an edge · from the map while walking · by a known point) and With two phones (DGPS · acoustic rangefinder) are signposts. "Why ±4 m?" shows your current accuracy. The correction is called "True length from tape or rangefinder".
Point hunters are in Learn, Hidden points next to Restore deleted point, Distant points into AR in Base data.

Settings → Application (formerly Maintenance + the side More): four sections Help and guides · About the app · Backup · Space on the phone — guide, Does everything work?, Write to the author, history, sharing, administration, backup, device profile, free up space. Hidden points are in Data next to the job. The strip under the tabs leads straight to the Guide.

verze.nadpis: Translations completed: guides, Regulations, Practice tasks and Geo cards in five languages, the last Czech remnants
body: The "?" guides of the tools (110 texts), Regulations and tolerances, Practice tasks and Geo cards are in English, German, Polish, Spanish and Italian — not literal translations but texts written according to what the tool does. The Czech originals stay unchanged (data/navody-xx.json, predpisy-xx.json, ulohy-xx.json).

Over 1,000 more texts translated from screens that used to stay Czech in a foreign language: Precise GPS, Calibration by walking along an edge, Correction from the map, Acoustic rangefinder, Axis, Layers, Quiz, Yearbook, My activity, GNSS forecast, Weather (notes on weights and ČHMÚ measurements), company panel, briefing. Sentences glued together with numbers ("38.6 m to the north-east", "September 2026", "Week: 6 min in the app…") via patterns.
Spanish and Italian caught up with the remaining 27 texts (account, sign-in, Cadastre); all five languages now have the same set of 6,539 keys.

The app in a foreign language no longer clings to the old dictionary: dictionary extensions and localised files are refreshed in the background on every start (before, the service worker kept them forever in the first downloaded form — new translations never reached you).
New test test_jazyky_data (53 checks: files per language, same structure and HTML, Italian guide in the "?" window, Regulations, tasks, cards) in CI.

verze.nadpis: Walk-through of the app, round 2: a new user gets in, the menu no longer taps into nothing
body: New user: gate → More options → "Create for this device only" → after closing the guide the app starts. Before, a black screen with only the dock remained (the company was created but nobody started the app).

More menu: "Task guide" and "Tutorial and tour" tapped right after start (before the deferred modules download) open a moment later — before, the tap silently fell through (openPruvodce / startTutorial is not defined).
Point card in a foreign language: "I found it — 40 m to go / stand still 5 s more / waiting for GPS" translated (it used to stay in Czech).

Passed: the gate and company creation, all menu items (Pro and Basic), every switch in Settings there and back, the Map panel rows, five languages, landscape display, gloves / left hand / font 130 % / outdoor / simple mode, 64 tools + 29 signpost items — no page error, no "undefined/NaN" text.

verze.nadpis: Daily check: Save and next fills in GPS by itself again
body: After "Save and next" the coordinates of the next point fill in from the GPS average by themselves again — even if you overwrote Y/X by hand at the previous point. Otherwise just a check: all 45 test suites green, password recovery tried live on the server (a one-off account, deleted after the test).

verze.nadpis: New point in two taps, bigger targets in the map, account recovery code
body: New point in two taps: after opening, the coordinates fill in from the GPS average by themselves and refine every second ("averaged from N · ±x m"); tapping "From GPS average" is no longer needed. Whoever overwrites Y/X by hand or picks the map or a photo switches the automation off. When there is no satellite fix yet, the note below the buttons says so — no pop-up.
Point markers in the map catch taps within a 28 px radius (was 25), in gloves mode 34 px.

Account recovery code: registration still needs no e-mail, but the account gets a second key (20 characters) when created. On the gate there is "Forgotten password? I have a recovery code" → new password without e-mail; after use you get a new code. Whoever has an older account makes a code in About → Account → Recovery code (asks for the password).
The regression tests in CI run in three streams (≈7 minutes instead of 20); two suites that occasionally timed out in the long batch now wait more reliably.

verze.nadpis: Walk-through of the whole app: what misbehaved when clicking through all the tools
body: The toast "Something went wrong (ucty:usageLog)" is gone. The storage overview in Settings → Maintenance created the modules' databases empty, and the module then couldn't write to them (change journal, usage measuring, photos, voice notes). The overview creates nothing anymore and each module adds its missing store itself — the data stays.
Site sketch: the "Move" button has an icon (it used to say "undefined").

Point card: an official point without Y/X in the data (e.g. Slovak points) shows S-JTSK computed from the position instead of dashes; on a small display (320 px) the coordinates aren't shortened with an ellipsis.
Distant points into AR: the "Collapse" wheel no longer lies over the status pill. Cadastre window: the wheel doesn't lie over the heading.
Terrain route without signal says "no signal, or the server isn't responding" instead of the English "Failed to fetch".
The CI test for Write to the author counted on three languages — since v351 there are five (so it was red).

verze.nadpis: Navigation without a pop-up, the map in one place, clearer Tools, the Controls tab, small displays, translations
body: Take me there without a pop-up: when the terrain route has no data right now (downloading, the target is too far…), an unobtrusive pill at the bottom of the map says so and disappears by itself — before, a window with an OK button in the middle of walking. Clearing the selection of distant points no longer overrides a download from ČÚZK still finishing.

The vector map has one place: it is switched on and styled only in the Map panel (Layers button → Base). In Settings → Data only the address of your own data remains. 3D view, Where can I measure and Site sketch no longer send you to Settings — they switch the map on themselves (or ask and switch it on).

Tools from four layers to two: the "What are you doing today" strip is gone from the Tools window (pick the work profile in Settings → Profiles; whoever wants the strip switches it on there too), ★ Pinned shows only when something is pinned, and the four office verbs (Before leaving, Company, Handbook, Learn) are sections on the "More" page — the strip has 8 verbs instead of 14. A new user opens Tools straight on Measure.
Settings → Controls: a new tab for left hand, gloves, vibration, gestures, simple mode, simplification and weaker phone / battery saving. Appearance keeps the theme, font and on-screen elements.
Small display and phone in landscape: on heights up to 640 px the dock rises and shrinks, so the Map/Split/AR wheel no longer lies over the Settings button (iPhone SE, 844×390).

Translations: 190 texts of tools from the latest versions (Point hunters, Precise GPS, Site sketch, Map panel, point card, measuring country…) added to English, German, Polish, Spanish and Italian; a CI check makes sure every new tool has a translation.
Messages like "You can revert the mode choice in Settings → Appearance" lead where the choice really is (Profiles, Controls).

verze.nadpis: Check after two days of changes: messages don't hold you up, map data doesn't hammer the server
body: The messages "Terrain route: …", "Obstacle saved", "Slovakia: N points" and "Layer hidden" are now short bubbles, not windows you have to dismiss (they also blocked dragging the divider in split).
When there's no map data for the country or no signal, the app tries again only after a minute (was every 5 s) and gives the real reason in the message.
All test suites passed: Map panel, terrain route, 3D, sketch, Geo cards, Slovak points, countries, Android, app walk-through.

verze.nadpis: Slovak official points, Geo cards refreshed, an airier Map panel, 3D by theme, house numbers upright
body: Slovakia has official points: when the measuring country is SK, GKÚ SR points within 1.2 km are downloaded — the State trigonometric network (I–V order, orientation and densification points), the levelling network, the gravimetric and spatial network — with designation, cadastral unit, mark type and Bpv height. In the map, in AR and in navigation they behave like Czech ones (they don't have the official ČÚZK sketch, of course). The position is converted from S-JTSK (±1 m).
Geo cards (formerly "Scroll and learn"): each kind has its own colour, a big icon and a subtle pattern, the content lies on paper; at the bottom is a card counter.

Map panel: a slimmer header, tabs with breathing room; in the Layers tab there's a new Surroundings watcher switch (you're standing in a building, by a wall, under trees…) and a link to the correction settings (walking calibration, correction from map, snapping to corners). In split the panel closes after choosing a base so you can see the map switched.
3D view follows the app theme (dark = night map), not the manually chosen 2D map style; blueprint and print stay.
House numbers, names of settlements and peaks in the vector map stay upright when the map rotates with your heading — you don't read them upside down (street names run along the street as on paper).
Map data: Austria uploaded (from the country outline, 1.0 GB) and Hungary.

verze.nadpis: The app speaks Spanish and Italian
body: Two new languages: Spanish and Italian. Everything that is in English, German and Polish is translated — the core and the whole extension (over 6,600 texts), including technical terminology (replanteo / tracciamento, distancias de control / misure di controllo, catastro / catasto…). Switch at the very top of Settings → Appearance or with the ring on the sign-in screen; a phone set to Spanish or Italian picks the language itself.

As with the other languages: Czech downloads nothing extra, the extension (~480 kB) is downloaded only after choosing the language and only that one. Proper names stay — ČÚZK, ČHMÚ, CZEPOS, S-JTSK, Bpv, decree numbers.

verze.nadpis: Map panel on three levels, terrain navigation even on orthophoto, obstacle on its own canvas
body: The Map and layers panel (Layers button) has three tabs: Base (Map · Vector · Orthophoto cards with a sample, below them map rotation, vector map style and measuring country), Layers (cadastre, parcels, drawing, GPS quality, obstacles, terrain route, own base — switches) and Tools (Look around · Draw and measure · Data on the phone). Only one level is visible at a time, swipe to the next. The temporary "Map trial" button is gone — everything from it has its place in the panel.

The terrain route works on orthophoto and on raster too — building and path data is taken from the map tiles regardless of what is visible right now (before only with the vector map switched on on screen → a straight line). When the data isn't there yet, the app says it's downloading and computes the route by itself.

Obstacle: drawn on its own canvas above the map, so it doesn't fight with panning, zooming or long press (measuring); two fingers in drawing mode pan and zoom the map. The shape is visible during the stroke and after saving; the enabled Obstacles layer can be hidden.
A vector map switched on from the 3D view or from the panel stays on even after a style change (before it switched off after switching the style).

verze.nadpis: From phone feedback: 3D card over the view, pavements on the terrain, obstacle by finger, sketch in a new coat, Scroll and learn
body: 3D view: tapping a point slides out the classic point card over the 3D (nothing switches to 2D, no flicker); a point is hit even 14 px off. Pavements are no longer broken rectangles — they are strips at real width with a kerb, laid on the terrain, without flicker and slanted slopes. Greenery is taken also from land-use areas (a park with trees, an orchard), before only from land cover — which is why it wasn't visible. The globe shows earlier (from the view of the whole of Czechia); MapLibre can't do more curvature than the real Earth's.

Obstacle: pick the kind and trace the shape with one finger in the map (two fingers = panning and zooming still work), no pop-ups; two taps = a rectangle as before. Cancel with the button in the bar at the top.

Terrain route: when there's no route and a straight line is shown, the app says why (target farther than 3 km, map loading, no passage from here…); range raised from 1.5 to 3 km. Underpasses and passages through buildings (a path in a tunnel) stay passable — only metro, railway and long road tunnels are dropped.

Site sketch: a new look (header with the point, base switch, palette of symbols at the bottom, bar with icons, north arrow, gridded paper) and symbols following thematic-map conventions (ČSN 01 3411, simplified): deciduous and coniferous tree, bush, post, lamp, manhole, hydrant, gully, boundary stone, traffic sign; lines fence / wall / kerb / ditch. Trees from the orthophoto: crown positions estimated from the ČÚZK orthophoto extent (dark or textured green patches) — added dashed, delete what doesn't fit.
Scroll and learn (Tools → Learn): cards to swipe — terms, formulas, regulations, questions from exercises, what the app can do, tips from the field; filter, star, counter.

Outside Czechia: map data for Slovakia, Hungary and Austria (Austria and Slovenia still uploading), the country simulation adds 3 sample points, the point list explains that ČÚZK official points exist only in Czechia.

verze.nadpis: Navigation no longer goes through walls, gravity point correct, working in 3D, site sketch
body: The terrain route takes buildings and paths straight from the map tiles for the whole section, not just what the map has on screen right now (zoomed-out map = no buildings = a route through houses). It keeps a metre away from buildings, follows paths along their axis (not a metre beside), grid 1 m. When you stand inside a building, it leads you first to the exit (entrance from the map, otherwise the side facing the street — not an emergency exit) and only from there over the terrain. A target in a closed courtyard or a building = the route ends at the nearest spot and shows the rest straight (red dashed). Metro and tunnels aren't used in the route.
AR: the arrow leads to the next vertex of the route, the line in the tape shows the sought point (direct direction) and the azure dot below it the next vertex.

A gravity point downloaded by an older version (saved as PPBP) is reclassified by the ČÚZK layer after a new download — a hexagon in the map and "Gravity point" in the card header, not a circle with PPBP.
Where can I measure: hide the layer with the "Hide" pill right in the map (or the button in the result dialog), not only in the Layers panel.

Obstacles in the map: before drawing you pick the kind (pile, excavation, machine, fence, water, storage, other) — each has a colour and a symbol, the name is written right in the map and can be renamed; an excavation on a path closes that path for the route.

3D view: tapping a point = a card with the buttons Point card and Navigate (the route is drawn in 3D too, after closing it keeps running in split), pavements 12 cm above the road (you can tell whether a point is on the pavement or in the road), points at height as a post from the DMR 5G terrain, greenery (forest, scrub) as volumes, when zooming out a globe; the light theme works.

New tool Site sketch (Cadastre and bases): for the selected point outlines from the map (buildings, roads, paths, water, rails, forest), dimensions from-to with two taps (length from coordinates, tap to enter the tape value), objects (tree, bush, post, manhole, hydrant, stone, sign), fence / edge, text; base Paper / Map / Orthophoto — what you draw on one you see on the others. Saved with the point, PNG export with north arrow, scale bar and legend.
Foreign country simulation (Settings → Data → Measuring country → Try): puts you in the capital of the chosen country — coordinates, heights, cadastre and map switch as in the field.
The strip under the status bar (Dynamic Island) no longer stays light after switching from light to dark mode.

verze.nadpis: Point sketch laid on the map — which side of the fence the point is on
body: Lay the sketch on the map — a button under the official ČÚZK sketch in the card of an official point. Tap the point mark in the sketch, then a building corner or boundary vertex, and the same corner in the map (within 3 m it snaps to a cadastral vertex). The sketch is stretched and rotated onto the cadastre, semi-transparent — you see which side of the post, fence or corner the point is on.

In AR the laid sketch is projected on the ground around the point; the bar at the bottom holds transparency, the AR switch, "Refine with another corner" (from three pairs it shows how much the points disagree) and "Take off". The placement survives a restart.

Honestly: sketches tend to be schematic → the surroundings fit to ±0.5–1 m, it's for "which side", not "where to dig". A corner from DKM is centimetres, from UKM ±1 m. The Point sketch on the map tile is in Tools → Cadastre and bases, with a guide.

verze.nadpis: Vector map data: the whole of Czechia available right away; temporary "Map trial" button
body: The whole of Czechia as map data (1.7 GB) lives in the GitHub release "mapa-data" and the QTRIG cloud reads it in pieces — so New map (vector, beta) can be switched on right away, without setting up Cloudflare. Once R2 with all of Europe exists, the worker will reach there itself; outside Czechia the map says for now that data for that country isn't there yet (file per country: sk.pmtiles, at.pmtiles…).

The "Map trial" button at the bottom left of the main screen (temporary): a signpost to everything the own map is built on — switch on the map and style, 3D view, Where can I measure, a sample DXF drawing around you (axis with chainage), obstacle, a trial target round the corner with a terrain route, surroundings watcher, edge correction, snapping to corners, measuring country, clean-up. Each item says where you'll find it permanently. Hide it with the cross (back: Settings → Appearance → Map).
When there's no data for the country, the map says so right away and the base stays raster.

verze.nadpis: Surroundings watcher, route to a point by terrain with a height profile, manual obstacles, cadastre and orthophoto of neighbouring countries
body: Surroundings watcher. By a building (within 4 m), inside a building by the map, under trees, by rails or by a marked obstacle the pill at the top tells you what it does to GPS and what to do ("move 10 m away, or step offset"). A new point from GPS records the conditions it was created in (e.g. "2.1 m from a building"). Switch off: Settings → AR & accuracy.

Obstacle with two taps. A pile of material, an excavation, an excavator — none of that is in any map. Layers → Map tools → Obstacle, tap two opposite corners: the route goes around it, the watcher warns before it, the GPS quality map shades it. Valid for the job; tap the rectangle to delete it.

Route to a point by terrain. Instead of a straight line a polyline that goes around buildings, water, motorways and obstacles and prefers paths over fields and forest (grid 2 m, computed on the phone). The tape and arrow in AR lead to the nearest vertex, the distance is the length along the route; if you stray 15 m it recomputes. Tapping the route shows the height profile (↑ climb, ↓ descent, steepest section). Switch off: Settings → AR & accuracy.

Cadastre and orthophoto outside Czechia. By the country you're standing in, the map bases switch: Slovakia (ESKN, ZBGIS), Poland (GUGiK), Austria (BEV, basemap.at), Netherlands (PDOK), France (IGN), Switzerland (swisstopo), Slovenia, Belgium (Flanders), Hungary, Spain (orthophoto). Elsewhere in the world Esri orthophoto. Honestly: foreign control networks aren't publicly available as data — outside Czechia you run on your own points, cadastre and map.
The vector map now checks before switching on that the data really is in the cloud; if not, it says why instead of showing an empty map.

verze.nadpis: Accuracy from the map: snapping a point to a corner, automatic GPS correction by an edge, "where can I measure" map
body: Snapping to corners. You save a GPS point within 0.6 m of a parcel boundary vertex (cadastre), a DXF drawing point or within 1 m of a building corner from the vector map → the app asks and takes the coordinates from the map instead of the phone. The point records where it came from (snapped to…), accuracy by source (cadastre 0.1 m, drawing 0.05 m, building 0.5 m). Switch off: Settings → AR & accuracy.

GPS correction by the edge you walk along. When you walk ≥ 20 m parallel to a parcel boundary, a building wall or a drawing line and GPS keeps you constantly the same distance beside it (spread under 0.9 m), it isn't your track but a GPS error: the app offers a shift perpendicular to the edge (or switches it on right away in "auto" mode). The same correction as "GPS shift to a known point" — pill at the top, watched for 20 min / 300 m. Road axes from OSM aren't used (±1–3 m). Mode in Settings → AR & accuracy.

Where can I measure (Tools → Precise measuring): a GPS quality map 220 × 220 m around you from shading by buildings (heights from OSM) and forest — green open sky, amber half the sky (measure longer), red by a wall (offset, another spot). An estimate, not a measurement; hide the layer in the Layers panel.
All three need the vector map switched on (Settings → Appearance) — the building data comes from it; parcels from the Parcels (vector) tool, the drawing from Project import.

verze.nadpis: GPS correction from the map while walking, a nicer website, a message after downloading a new version
body: New tool GPS correction from the map while walking (Precise measuring): stand still 30–60 s, tap the orthophoto exactly where you stand and the app subtracts the GPS error even while walking — in AR, in navigation, in distances and in saved points. Valid 10 min / 100 m, the pill at the top watches. The static "Position from map" stays separate. A card in the Precise measuring guide + a guide under "?".
The app's website has a new look (stepanvcelak11.github.io/ar-geodet/web/).
After downloading a new version the pill says the app must be closed and started again.

verze.nadpis: Own vector map (beta): "construction" style, DXF drawing as a layer with chainage, 3D view
body: New map (vector, beta) — Settings → Appearance. The base is no longer someone else's image but our OpenStreetMap data in one file that the phone fetches in pieces. "Construction" style: buildings with house numbers, road edges, rails, water, forest and fields, boundaries — no shops or ads. Four variants from one data set: day, night (really dark), blueprint, print (black and white for PDF); "by theme" switches by itself.

Drawing (DXF) as a map layer. Project import draws lines in the CAD layer colours, keeps polylines as wholes and in the tool you pick a layer as the axis: chainage marks run along it and tapping any line tells the layer, length and chainage ("km 0.420" · 3.2 m from the axis). The "Drawing (DXF)" row in the Layers panel hides/shows it.

3D view (Tools → Cadastre and bases): buildings extruded to height, terrain, job points, the drawing and my position from an oblique angle. Two fingers rotate and tilt; tapping a building, point or line tells what it is. Needs the vector map switched on.

Map data: the file is being uploaded to the QTRIG cloud (Cloudflare R2, instructions in cloud/wrangler.toml); until then you can enter your own address in Settings (an extract from scripts/mapa-vyrez.py — Czechia is 1.7 GB). Without signal the vector map doesn't run yet (area download is coming); OSM raster and orthophoto stay as before.
In weaker-phone mode the vector map and 3D aren't offered (WebGL, a 1 MB library).

verze.nadpis: Android: the Back button closes windows instead of the app, "Add to home screen" offer
body: The Back button on Android closes the topmost open window (Tools, point card, dialog…) — before, in the app on the home screen it quit the app straight away. On the main screen the first Back warns, a second within 2.5 s closes the app, as is customary on Android.
Add QTRIG to the home screen: Chrome on Android offers installation once after a minute in the app (full screen, own icon, offline). "Not now" = quiet for 14 days.

The whole app went through Chrome emulation on Android (Pixel 7 and a 360 px display, compass from deviceorientationabsolute without permission, relative events ignored, 102 Tools tiles without error and without any element off-screen) — the test runs in CI.

verze.nadpis: Measuring outside Czechia: coordinates and heights by the country you stand in; EGM2008 geoid and WMM declination for the whole world
body: The app recognises the country from GPS and switches the coordinate system. In Czechia everything stays as before (S-JTSK Y/X, Bpv). In Slovakia S-JTSK [JTSK03], in Poland PL-2000 (X/Y, zone by longitude), in Germany ETRS89/UTM (E/N), in Austria MGI GK (M28/M31/M34), Hungary EOV, Switzerland LV95, France Lambert-93, Netherlands RD, Belgium Lambert 72, Britain OSGB, Slovenia, Croatia, Spain, Scandinavia, the Baltics, Romania, Bulgaria… and elsewhere in the world generic UTM. Point card, point form, list, CSV/TXT/DXF/PDF export, calculators, stake-out, reports — all in that country's plane.

Heights in the national system. The geoid undulation now comes from the EGM2008 model (all of Europe at 5′, the world at 1°), plus the offset of the national height system against EVRF2007: Bpv, DHHN2016, GHA (Adriatic), NAP, TAW, LN02, NGF-IGN69, ODN… For countries where I don't know the offset, ±0.5 m is shown. A fix for Czechia too: the previous formula fitted in Prague, but in Brno it was 1.7 m off and in the corners of the country 3–8 m.
Declination anywhere in the world. The compass is corrected by the World Magnetic Model 2025 (NOAA) — before a linear estimate for Czechia that would lie by 6° in Spain.

Settings → Data → Measuring country. Automatically by GPS (country outlines are accurate to ~1 km — near a border switch by hand), or a fixed chosen country. When crossing a border the app says what it switched to.
What DOESN'T change: ČÚZK official points, RÚIAN parcels, VFK and GML networks always stay in Křovák — they are Czech data.
The data (geoid ~740 kB, outlines ~170 kB) is downloaded once after start and stays on the phone; until then the Czech formulas run as in v338.

verze.nadpis: Gravity points separately, numbers of associated points, tapping a parcel with territory protection, walking calibration along a cadastral boundary, download animation
body: Gravity points have their own symbol — an orange hexagon in the map and in AR, the card says "Gravity point · name". They used to look like trigonometric points (purple triangle). They aren't offered for GPS anchoring (they tend to be in buildings).

Associated (witness) points of TB and ZhB have a number with a sequence: 19.3, 19.4 — before, three points "19" stood next to each other in the map. The TB card has a new row with the triangulation sheet.
Fix: labels of cancelled points from the ČÚZK service showed as valid detail points.

Tapping a parcel shows more: the area from graphics next to the official one, boundary source (DKM to centimetres / UKM to metres), validity, nearest address, terrain height from DMR 5G, for a building the construction, floor area and year of completion. New section Protection and restrictions: BPEJ (decoded), NP / protected landscape area / reserve / monument with their buffer zones, Natura 2000, memorial tree, protected deposit area, mining area and the protection zone of a fundamental control point mark.

Walking calibration along a cadastral boundary: with the Cadastre layer on, a tap within 4 m of a parcel boundary snaps to the nearest spot on the boundary — the outline is downloaded from RÚIAN by itself. In UKM territory the app reckons with ±1 m.

Point card: the "Status: not staked" tile is gone, the Staked button stays only with own points. Below the buttons a sentence says how Check point (just a record of where I stand) and Correct GPS (shifts further measurements) differ.

Correct GPS warns about where you stand: under a tree, by a wall or between houses GPS has a different error than in the open — when the position wavers, the app says so and advises another point or a longer average.

DGPS more precisely: the base block is the median of fixes weighted by reported accuracy, the rover weights fresh blocks more and drops an outlying block. The tool now says why it can't reach centimetres.
You can see the new version downloading: "Downloading new version… 42 %" with a bar appears at the top, a tick when done. When a new version is deployed, a spinning wheel after start.
New app website: stepanvcelak11.github.io/ar-geodet/web/ — what the app can do, samples, Basic and Pro, accuracy honestly, installation.

verze.nadpis: GPS correction by a known point also for height, levelling points in the list, Correct GPS square in the point card
body: The height is corrected too. If the point you stand on has a Bpv height (levelling benchmark, many TB and ZhB), the "GPS shift to a known point" tool computes the vertical shift too and adds it to the height of newly saved points from the GPS average. Put the phone on the mark, or write how much higher you hold it. A height overwritten from the DEM is left alone.
Levelling points are in the list. Their position at ČÚZK is to a metre — still better than the phone — and the height to millimetres.

Correct GPS straight from the point card. Among the card buttons there's a "Correct GPS" square: the confirmation tells you how far from the point you are by GPS, whether the point has a height and that you must stand right on it — then the correction switches on with one tap. The tool in Tools stays.
Fix: a confirmation window opened from the point card (like this very one) couldn't be confirmed — the tap closed the card instead of confirming.

verze.nadpis: Icons instead of emoji everywhere
body: All the places where the app used emoji instead of an icon (Where's my stuff, badges in the Yearbook, Step offset, Campaign, Sun and light, radar in Weather, Newsletter, Defects, voice notes, the clock at points, guides…) now have the app's icons — the same on iPhone and Android, correct in the light theme too. Emoji remain only in the avatar symbol picker (that's your choice, not an icon).

verze.nadpis: Distant points into AR: pick the area even from home, points get fetched from ČÚZK and are in the map too
body: Pan and zoom the map in the tool with two fingers — you don't have to stand in that area. Select the rectangle either by dragging with one finger as before, or by tapping one corner and then the opposite one (between taps feel free to pan the map further).

Points in the extent get fetched from ČÚZK. The app normally downloads control points only within 300 m of you, so an extent 2 km away used to report "no point". Now the control points are downloaded and selected for it; without signal at least what the phone already has is taken.
Selected points are drawn in the map too, not just in AR — even kilometres from you. The extent and corners are visible right in the map while selecting.

verze.nadpis: App walk-through — 11 fixes from clicking through all the tools
body: GNSS forecast showed in the Geo-photo window after it had been opened (both modules had the same window id) — each has its own now; a similar pair Measuring procedures × First measurement guide (one of them stayed unstyled).
Does everything work? reported "Basic" for the account even with Pro (it called a non-existent licence function).
Track log opened with an empty button and no statistics until the next GPS fix arrived.
Yearbook: the row of months began "Jan Jan" and December was missing.

Day journal: five buttons didn't fit in a row on a narrow phone ("Close" cut off); Offset point: the azimuth field was squeezed to a few pixels; Parcel: two crosses on top of each other; Quiz: a cut-off caption under the drawing; Sun and light: a row label wrapped onto three lines; the "Download within a radius of300 m" slider without a space; Settings → Profiles: a clipped "Who are you" selection.
Light theme: yellow warnings (Polar point, Intersection, Free station, guide, point card…) were unreadable on white — now dark; the header of the Tie distances table is no longer a dark strip.
GNSS forecast: instead of "Measure 20:00–20:00" (the whole window) it says "any time in the next 24 h".

verze.nadpis: Point card: map sheet instead of the "all official records" expander
body: The "Show all official records" expander is gone from the point card. It was a raw dump from ČÚZK and everything in it (number, cadastral unit, accuracy class, heights, line, name, link to geodetic data) is already shown at the top of the card in readable form.
New Map sheet row — the only thing that was only in the raw dump: the ZM 1:50 000 and SMO-5 sheet (name + number), below the heights and geoid undulation.

verze.nadpis: Tools are paged: one verb = one page, Mine first, Pro aside; the tool wheel dropped
body: Tools as pages. Instead of one column across seven screens there's a strip of verbs at the top (Measure · New point · Measure precisely · Stake out · …) and below it always one page that fits the display. Page by swiping sideways or tapping a verb; the bottom says what is left and right.

The Mine page is first: Continue (last used tool), work type choice, ★ Pinned and For this work. Pin a tool with the star right in its row. A pinned tool shows its gesture (or "+ gesture" to draw one) — the panel is thus also a gesture cheat sheet.

Signposts (Point by computation, Align otherwise, GNSS signal, Bases and cadastre, Weather and light, Day record, My numbers, Handbook) expand in place under their row, not into another window. Every row has a "?" with a guide, so you can explore without opening.

In Basic, Pro is aside. Locked tools from the paid version aren't scattered among the verbs — they gathered on the last "Pro" page (with the verb in the title) so they don't get in the way. Whoever has Pro doesn't see that page.

The tool wheel (holding the Tools button) dropped. Three paths led to a tool and it was complicated; two remain: Tools for paging and exploring, gestures for launching from memory. Holding the button now does the same as tapping.

verze.nadpis: The point card says which GPS correction was added to the point
body: The point card has a new GPS correction tile for GPS points: by how much and from where the point was shifted (walking along an edge, known point, live DGPS, correction from QR) and whether it was recomputed by before-and-after calibration. The accuracy explanation ("where the accuracy came from") says the same — before, the card claimed "only what the phone reports" even about a point that calibration had moved half a metre back into place.
Recomputing points by time (before-and-after calibration) no longer forgets where the correction came from, and the point card sees it right away.

verze.nadpis: Precise measuring — a new section in Tools: walk around a shape, before-and-after calibration, where to put the phone, temporary DGPS base
body: The Precise measuring section in Tools: everything that squeezes accuracy out of the phone, together — Precise GPS, Calibration by walking along an edge, GPS shift to a known point, Two-phone DGPS, Acoustic rangefinder and Check measurement. At the head How to measure precisely with a phone: three GPS errors (noise, shift, drift), what each method solves, a "what to expect" table, a 3–5 step procedure for each method, where calibration works and where it doesn't, and typical situations (paving by a kerb, a plot, a field without a point). Each tool also has a short "Simply" at the top.

Walking calibration: walk around a shape. The line can be closed (Close shape button or a tap back to the first point) — a plot's perimeter, a plus, a square — and the whole error vector comes out, not just the component perpendicular to a line. The app now shows how much the GPS error drifted during the walk (first vs. second half; for a loop the same as the misclosure) and warns above 1 m.

Before-and-after calibration. When you walk the edge again within 90 minutes and 500 m, the app says by how much the GPS error shifted in between and offers to recompute by measurement time the points saved between the two walks (even from Precise GPS) — a point in the middle gets half the difference. The vector is replaced, not added; the changes go into the journal.

The correction is as accurate as the line's source: the app remembers the source (orthophoto ±0.35 m, cadastral boundary ±0.3 m, saved points ±cm, street map ±2 m — that one it discourages right away and advises switching to orthophoto) and adds it to the error estimate as "total". A tap within 4 m of a vertex of a downloaded parcel snaps to the cadastral boundary.

Precise GPS: where to put the phone. A picture of the phone with a cross — the centre belongs over the point, the antenna is at the top edge and rotating by 90° around the centre cancels its position out. The correction added is saved with the point (for the before/after recomputation). After saving the app offers the point as a temporary DGPS base for a second phone.

Two-phone DGPS: temporary base. The base can also be a point from Precise GPS with walking calibration — the window says what that gives (rover points ±0.5 m relative to each other, the whole inherits the base's error as a common shift, walking calibration thereby lasts longer) and what it doesn't (extra accuracy). The acoustic rangefinder in intersection from two GPS points says the shape is to centimetres and the position of the whole follows the known points.

verze.nadpis: Tapping a parcel, the official ČÚZK sketch in the point card, tools back in sight
body: Parcel on tap: switch on the Cadastral map layer in the map and tap inside a parcel — a card from RÚIAN shows number, cadastral unit, municipality, area, land type, use and a possible building (house number, storeys, built-up area); the outline is highlighted. No free service gives the owner and title deed — the Owner and title deed button opens this very parcel in the ČÚZK cadastre viewer.

Official point card: instead of the app's sketch there's now the official ČÚZK site sketch from the point's geodetic data (tie distances to house corners, fences…), for TB/ZhB an extract from the sheet with a switch to the whole sheet; the link to the full geodetic data remains. The app's sketch (neighbouring points, tie distances) is one tap below it. Own points keep it. A sketch once shown works without signal too.

Tools: Tie distances, Track log and Today in the field no longer hide from a new installation; the signpost rows (Align otherwise, Bases and cadastre, GNSS signal, Handbook…) list all their items, so even a new tool in them can be found without searching.
Status bubble: a warning with numbers no longer jumps from left to right (the azimuth, cut off because of the message 5× a second, kept coming back and disappearing).

Point hunters and Download area without comparisons to a mobile game; the buttons of the new tools (Acoustic rangefinder, Calibration by walking along an edge, DGPS) have the app's icons instead of emoji.

verze.nadpis: Free up space on the phone
body: Settings → Maintenance → Free up space: an overview of what the app keeps on the phone — the downloaded map (tiles from Save surroundings, Pack the job and Download area, with an MB estimate) and each downloaded district/region separately — and Delete at each item. Deleting an area takes its map tiles too; the "Used X MB" row recalculates at once.

verze.nadpis: Smoothness round 2 — faster start, a map without jerks while walking, Tools without freezing
body: Start on a weaker phone: deferred modules are now deployed minified (3.0 MB → ~1.2 MB; shorter update download and parsing), in Weaker phone mode they're fetched two at a time and only when idle; the three student tools download only on tap.

Measuring dimensions only after rendering: the status strip, notifications, window closing, mini-panel and work mode used to measure elements in the middle of an unfinished layout (about 0.7 s of main thread in the first seconds). Now they measure once after the frame and only when something changed.

The map redraws only the difference: markers that stay aren't deleted and rebuilt — redrawing 200 markers 96–177 ms → 5–28 ms, walking 60 m without six freezes. Tapping a marker is no longer lost by the marker being swapped under the finger.

Tools: the grid is assembled once after the batch of registrations instead of a hundred times at start; on opening only the tiles on screen are laid out. Opening: 11 long tasks (1.3 s, one of them 0.54 s) → one under 0.2 s (weak phone).
Map first, markers after the frame: after start the map and position appear, markers are added in small batches.
Weaker phone: map tiles load only after the pan finishes and with a smaller buffer beyond the edge.

verze.nadpis: DGPS live over the internet and more precise walking calibration (there and back)
body: Two-phone DGPS live (Pro): the base on a known point taps Share corrections live and shows a six-character code; the second phone enters the code in Live from the internet and from then on the current correction is added to every saved point (also in Brutal GPS) — no more waiting for a QR. The pill at the top reports data age and distance from the base (limits 6 min / 3 km), Disconnect offers a retroactive correction of older points. Range ~2–3 km, needs internet on both phones (the base sends ~4 kB per minute).

Calibration by walking along an edge is more precise: fixes are weighted by their accuracy (±3 m has 16× more say than ±12 m) and when you walk the edge there and back, the app separates how far you hold the phone to the side of your track (in the right hand typically 0.2–0.4 m) — that used to stay in the correction. The correction error estimate accounts for per-second fixes not being independent.
The DGPS and walking calibration guides have been completed.

verze.nadpis: The GPS correction is watched: a pill at the top, a warning before expiry and at the distance limit
body: Watcher of GPS correction validity (from walking along an edge as well as from "GPS shift to a known point"): after switching on, a pill at the top shows "GPS correction 1.8 m · 12 min to go · 80 m from the spot" — green valid, amber nearing the limit, red beyond it. The app warns 5 min before expiry (20 min), after expiry, at 200 m from the calibration spot and at 300 m — each once. Tapping the pill opens the tool that made the correction; it doesn't switch itself off, the decision is yours.

Calibration by walking along an edge: a much longer explanation in the window — why it works (the same principle as DGPS), how it's computed, what accuracy you can reach (30–50 m of walking → ±0.3–0.5 m perpendicular to the edge, with a good signal ±0.2 m; a line from the map adds the base's error) and how long it's valid. The result says right away how accurate new points will be; a switched-on correction in the window shows the remaining minutes and the distance from the calibration spot.

verze.nadpis: Point hunters — a collection of discovered points, awards and hunting
body: Point hunters (Tools → Aids): official points you actually reach in the field (within 5 m, GPS to 8 m, 15 s standing) and tap I found it in the card are saved into your collection. A discovered point has a gold star in the map. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Score by rarity in Czechia (from ČÚZK counts): TB 50 · ZhB 30 · levelling 10 · PPBP 3 · gravity 200. The collection shows how many points of the district you're missing (when the district is downloaded on the phone).

Awards: First stone, Dozen, Hundred, Triangle (3 TB from one triangulation sheet), Whole line (all points of a levelling line), District (all TB of the district), District summit, Stone from a building — with progress to the nearest one.
Hunt: the nearest undiscovered points within 2 km sorted by yield per metre walked, with a Take me there button; Stone of the day for double (the same for everyone in the district).

verze.nadpis: Two new ways to get a more precise position out of a bare phone — by sound and by walking
body: Acoustic rangefinder (Pro): the distance between two phones from sound, to centimetres. The phone on a known point answers with a beep, the other measures; each finds in its own recording when it beeped and when the other did (one sample = 7 mm of sound travel), the clock difference subtracts itself and the second phone "tells" its measured time by the gap between two beeps — no internet, no copying numbers. Distances to two known points → Point from two distances (intersection) without GPS. Inside there's an explanation and a procedure; the first time do the zero calibration at 2.00 m. Tools → Measuring.

Calibration by walking along an edge (Pro): tap in the map from where to where you'll walk (kerb, pavement edge, fence, an axis from DXF — or two saved points), enter the side offset and just walk. From the transverse deviations of the fixes the app computes how much GPS lies here and now, and Switch on correction adds it to new points like "GPS shift to a known point" — just without stopping. On a straight line only the component perpendicular to the line, on a polyline the whole vector. Tools → Align otherwise.
New guides under "?" at both tiles; point origin "acoustic rangefinder" in the point card.

verze.nadpis: A district, region or the whole of Czechia on the phone — points without loading; official points sorted correctly
body: Download area (Tools → Bases and cadastre): download all official points of a whole district, region or the republic (~635,000 points) plus an overview map. While walking, points are then taken from the phone instead of the network — they appear at once (12 ms instead of seconds) and work without signal. The download can be interrupted and finished later; packages can be updated and deleted.

Fix of official point classification: the app asked ČÚZK for layers the service had long ago renumbered — a trigonometric point showed as "densification", a densification point as "detail", and cancelled points looked valid. Now all 16 layers are read correctly (TB, ZhB, PPBP, ZVBP/PVBP levelling and gravity points) and cancelled ones aren't shown.

The official point card now shows the point type, the full twelve-digit number (not just "28"), cadastral unit and district, accuracy class (PPBP), levelling line and, for points determined in ETRS89, the ellipsoidal height.

More precise height from GPS: for points determined in ETRS89, ČÚZK also knows the ellipsoidal height, so the app computes the real geoid undulation on the spot (to centimetres) instead of a formula with a 1–2 m error — transferring GPS height to Bpv is thereby more precise throughout the app (export, double measurement, point height).
Fewer requests to ČÚZK: one batch of points while walking = 1 request instead of 6 (same data). Easier for a weak signal too.
Language on the sign-in screen: after switching the language, sign-in, registration and the account code stayed in Czech — the texts were missing from the dictionary. Added (EN/DE/PL).

verze.nadpis: Gate without a hole, the owner's console holds, camera from Play with instructions
body: Fix: "More options" on the sign-in screen and Close right away could let you in without an account (the start safeguard saw "no gate"). The guide now brings the gate back at once and the safeguard treats it as a gate.
The error log no longer records unloaded map tiles (a moment without signal) — 18 of 20 records were this and real errors got buried among them. The same applies to Errors from people in the console.

Owner's console: when the server doesn't respond (weak signal, brake), the view stays open with the reason and "Try again" — before, an alert popped up and the console jumped to the signpost ("can't open it"). The "something's waiting" dot recalculates right after messages are handled. The "error at one person" watcher leads straight to their account. The errors tile has a label by the chosen period.

Camera from Google Play: when it's blocked, the instructions say where to allow it — in Chrome (phone Settings → Apps → Chrome → Camera and Chrome → Site settings → Camera), not in a non-existent address bar.

Who are you? when creating an account explains the Student / Surveyor / Company difference concretely (an employee = Surveyor and a code from the boss; Company = the boss who leads people) and advises: unsure → Surveyor.

verze.nadpis: Settings start with point range, the map rotates smoothly, taps aren't lost
body: Settings: the AR & accuracy tab is first and opens by default; right at the top is the Point range section with both sliders — visibility in the AR camera and point range in the map (that was hidden in the Data tab until now).

Map rotation no longer jerks: after settling, only the point labels on screen are straightened (others once they get there), and while walking the map redraws only when the set of points in range really changes.

Taps aren't lost: while your finger is on the display, the app doesn't rebuild what you're tapping — the point list, map markers and Settings don't redraw under the finger (that's why you sometimes had to tap twice).

verze.nadpis: The map rotates without tearing, the camera under tools doesn't go out, replying to a message
body: Map rotation: point labels straighten to horizontal only a moment after you stop turning — before, they were rewritten with every compass frame and on a weaker phone that took 79 % of performance (measured); now 0. While turning, labels are slanted for a fraction of a second.
AR markers are built only for points in range and only while the camera runs (before they were built for all job points, even in Map only mode): a fifth fewer elements on screen, faster start.
The Points window for a big job: the first 30 rows at once, the rest arrives calmly and while scrolling ("N more points…"); search finds a point from the end of the list too.

Tools and sensors: when measuring object height the camera went out (battery saving put it to sleep under the settings window). Tools now say themselves what they need — the camera, compass or GPS isn't put to sleep under them (object height, AR ruler, stamped photo, intersection from a photo, polar point, resection, stake-out, epochs, satellites, calibration…). Track recording keeps GPS even under the calculator or Settings.

A message from the author has a Reply button — the reply reaches the author's inbox and he can answer back into the app. Every message to the author now carries the account code, so an answer into the app works for all messages, not just Pro requests.

verze.nadpis: A smoother app: smaller point range and a mode for a weaker phone
body: Point range is smaller: official points (ČÚZK) are downloaded and shown in the map within 300 m of you (was 1 km) and in the AR camera within 100 m (was 150). Fewer markers = a smoother map and camera. Set both with a slider: Settings → Data → "Point range in the map" and Settings → AR & accuracy → "Point visibility in the AR camera". Own job points are always drawn in the map. Whoever had the old defaults 1000/150 m saved got the new ones; a custom range doesn't change.

Weaker phone (Settings → AR & accuracy): an economical display without glass, shadows and animations, camera 480p, compass 20× a second, at most 40 markers in AR. Switches on by itself on a phone with little memory or when the app measures it can't keep up; can be set manually to On / Off. Measuring and data are the same.
Share the app (QR) in the More panel is now seen only by the app owner. The app is meant to be downloaded from Google Play (testers via invitation), not from a QR as a web page.

verze.nadpis: The tool flower more readable and a return to the owner's console
body: Tool flower: all petals have the same font size, labels are wider and don't break mid-word; with twelve directions the petals don't overlap. The "Record" group has "Rec." on the petal (the full name is in the middle of the flower).

Owner's console: every view has one big "‹ Back to console" button at the top under the heading — always in the same place, it doesn't scroll away. Windows opened from the console (People, Messages, Companies…) have a gold "‹ Console" tab on the left edge. Returning after closing a window works with the camera running too.
Layers: the "Show target" tile is called "Show me and the target" — it fits the map so that both you and the point you're walking to are visible (it's there only while guiding).

verze.nadpis: A small thing: "Learn" has its own section in Tools
body: Trainer, Guess it, Exercises, Quiz and Formulas stand in the Tools grid under the heading "Learn", not in "Other".

verze.nadpis: Account deletion and clarified privacy — preparation for Google Play
body: Delete account right in the app: Settings → More → About → Delete account. It asks for the password, deletes the account and your own space on the server; points and jobs on the phone stay. Without the app you can request it on the smazani-uctu.html page.

About → Privacy says exactly what goes to the server (account data, anonymous usage records, error reports) and what doesn't (position, camera image). The privacy policy has been rewritten the same way.
A small thing: the link to the privacy policy and account deletion also in English, German and Polish.

verze.nadpis: Pro is free until the end of the year — just ask
body: The Pro version card says it straight: until the end of 2026 Pro is free, just send a request and the author switches it on; from 2027 Pro will be a subscription (monthly or yearly).

verze.nadpis: Owner's console, round two: an overview at a glance, search, notifications to the phone and thirteen new things
body: The console home screen is rearranged: search at the top, a "Since your last visit" block, a "this isn't normal" watcher (only when something deviates), summary numbers and Charts; below that five collapsible sections by what you're asking (What's happening · People, companies and messages · Releases and server · This phone · Key).
Search across the whole console: name, account code, company, a word from a message or error — accounts, companies, messages and errors one tap from the detail.
Notifications to the phone even with the app closed (new message, Pro request, wave of errors). On iPhone from the app on the home screen.
Charts 7 / 30 / 90 days with comparison to the previous period and CSV; Newcomer funnel (registration → first point → day 3 → rating, who dropped off).
Reply to a person straight into the app from the inbox; Person's diary day by day in "Through the account's eyes"; Releases shows who is on which version and who's stuck on an old one.

"Show me the app as Basic" for 15–60 minutes; Server status and capacity (requests and database against the free limits, how long it'll last); Clean-up of old data with a preview; Day summary 24 h / 3 days / since last time; Development report downloadable as .md.
Small things: the key lock says in how many minutes to try again; during a server outage the last known numbers stay with a label; on a computer the console is wider with four tiles in a row.

verze.nadpis: For students: Who are you?, Learn, Why ±4 m?, computation procedure — and 12 tools aside
body: Who are you? — Student / Surveyor / Company after the first entry (any time in Settings → Profiles). A student has the Learn group at the top of Tools and in accounts "crew" is said instead of "company".

Learn: Trainer and Guess it are in Basic; new Exercises (22 problems with a key, can be pre-filled into the Calculator), Point quiz (TB, levelling bolt, boundary stone, nail…) and Formulas in the Handbook.
Why ±4 m? — the error budget of GPS + compass over the distance to a point, with an ellipse and "what if" sliders; in GNSS signal and in the expanded status bubble.

The Calculator shows the computation procedure (formulas and intermediate results, even the bearing quadrant) and has the Helmert transformation. Fixed: a traverse with 2+ intermediate points computed wrongly (field id collision) and an empty field gave NaN instead of "Fill in".

Aside (find them via search): Epochs, volume by walking around, Localization as a tool, two of the three intersections, inside a building, paving layer + Paving profile, points on top of each other, travel log, safety, checklist (now a button in the Day journal).
Settings: colour tint, animations and bar curvature are in Advanced; the settings profile is collapsed under the work profile.

verze.nadpis: Take me there at the top of the point card, Charts within reach in the console, gold Pro only where it belongs
body: Point card: the buttons Take me there · Check point · Staked are right at the top, not below the sketch.

Owner's console: Charts — visual overview is the first tile and a gold button right under the summary numbers; the lock after wrong keys holds a quarter of an hour instead of an hour and the message advises switching Wi-Fi ↔ mobile data.
Pro at a glance toned down: only the Map/Split/AR switch and the Tools button with the PRO label are gold; Tools, headings and Settings are green again.

verze.nadpis: Cadastre with Back, owner's console without a false lock, gold Pro; walkie-talkie, attendance and the watch gone
body: Cadastre — where I stand right now opens in an app window with a Back button (iKatastr.cz map). Before it jumped to the browser and there was no way back. The Settings choice controls the "In browser" button.
Owner's console: "Too many key attempts, try in an hour" came even with the correct key — the server counted every console request as a guess. Now it counts only wrong keys.

Pro at a glance: the gold from the flower continues through the app — the pill at the top, the Map/AR switch, window headings, icons and headings in Tools, switches and tabs in Settings, the PRO label on the Tools button.

The status bubble can no longer be switched off (the "Turn off bubble" button and the switch in Settings are gone); the switches of the old panels, which had nothing to act on without it, are hidden too.

Gone: Walkie-talkie, Attendance (also the home-screen shortcut) and the Garmin watch — on request; we may come back to it in the future. The "Company" and "Transfers and devices" signposts disappeared with it; Company and accounts and Send/load job stand directly in the list.

verze.nadpis: The guide shows where to tap, the flower without needless signposts, the console with charts and a report
body: The first measurement guide now visibly ticks off every step and a "tap here" ring glows on the target (the + button, a point in the map, Take me there).
Tool wheel: signposts (Weather and light, GNSS signal…) unfold straight into petals when they fit; only what would overflow stays merged.
Basic × Pro has a simple visual overview at the top (five Pro areas), the long table is collapsed.

Owner: the console opens by itself only on the first entry; People have sorting and filters (last active, use the most, newest, With Pro, blocked); new Charts — 30 days and Development report (messages, ratings, errors and versions in one copyable text).
Languages: everything new (the guide, Does everything work?, rating, Where I work) and a few old leftovers are translated into EN/DE/PL.

Small things: windows no longer show through (History, Newsletter), readable field hints in the light theme, decimal comma in distances in point lists, Yearbook "Jun/Jul" and "1 day"; the contact from Write to the author is remembered with the account.

verze.nadpis: Before the beta: first measurement guide, Does everything work?, lighter start
body: First measurement guide on first launch: five steps over the live app (position and compass, accuracy, first point, its card, Take me there) — they tick themselves off. You'll also find it in the Interactive tutorial.
Does everything work? (Tools, Settings → Maintenance): GPS, compass, camera, storage, version and latest errors as green/red rows, one tap to the author.
Your contact (Where I work → Contact, optional) — the author has someone to ask when you send a report; Write to the author pre-fills it.
On the third day with the app it asks once "How does it suit you?" (stars + a sentence).
Start is 113 kB lighter (the tutorial, update history, coordinate list and task guide download only after the first frame).
The status pill no longer cuts off the message — azimuth and accuracy give way first.
Owner: app version, phone and contact at people in the console.

verze.nadpis: Check after the walk-through: two small things
body: Volumes and contours: the "Collapse" wheel lay right on the window's cross — now it stands next to it and a long heading wraps.
Sketch / tacheometry: the "there's more" fade on the button bar covered the last button (export) after scrolling.

verze.nadpis: App walk-through: the app is informal everywhere, version in About, small things
body: The app is informal everywhere — the last windows that were formal (Write to the author, point sharing, computations, compass calibration, storage warning…) speak like the rest. The EN/DE/PL translations match.
About shows the real version (it used to say "1.9" forever) and Update history has the v286–v299 entries filled in.
Point card: the "Point group" and "Nearby points" lists say that a tap opens the card (not navigation).
The Company and accounts guide no longer describes the abolished "limited mode"; the gate survives a tap on "More options" right after start.
The DTM window has a header and cross like other windows; the Pro card no longer has a needless "Collapse".
Status pill: "Continue: …" fits in it; a refused screen lock (background, power-saving mode) isn't reported as an error.
Basic in the Pro overview lists all free tools; the action bar in Tacheometry hints that it scrolls; the links at profiles have a bigger target; the date in the Newsletter is human-readable.

verze.nadpis: Search in Settings keeps the typed text, lighter start
body: Search in Settings deleted the first letters when you started typing right after opening — fixed.
The app start is 36 kB lighter: the point card content downloads only when the card is first opened.
The point card in the light theme is readable (it used to be white text on white).

verze.nadpis: Point card: sketch over the orthophoto, dragging by the strip
body: The surroundings sketch lies over the orthophoto with parcel boundaries (base from ČÚZK), neighbouring points within 150 m, tie distances and a scale bar.
