The height is shown for levelling points too — the ČÚZK control point data has it for all layers, the app used to overlook it for levelling.
Drag the point card by the strip up over the whole screen and back down.
Owner: a new version reaches others only after "Release to others" in the console — a release can be braked when something goes wrong.

verze.nadpis: The point card is an overview, not navigation
body: Tapping a point (in the map, in the cluster list, in Nearby points) opens the point card and doesn't navigate. Start navigation from the card with the Take me there button; Check point and Staked are available too.
The card as a mosaic: Y/X in large type with the kind icon, accuracy in colour, status, height, distance from me, when and from where measured, job, photos.
Survey sketch of the surroundings: neighbouring points, tie distances between them, parcels and a "you" marker when you're in the frame.

verze.nadpis: Face ID for the owner, company switching at sign-in
body: The app owner signs in with Face ID / fingerprint instead of copying a long key (offered after the first sign-in with the key).
Switch company is on the sign-in screen too — when the device knows several companies or spaces.
Owner: overview, diary, calendar, backup and a view through the account's eyes in the console; gold theme of the owner's windows.

verze.nadpis: App walk-through: fourteen fixes of what didn't work or didn't fit
body: Gate → "More options" was a dead screen (the start overlay lay over the guide) — it works.
The "Collapse" wheel in Field books ran over the Close button; signposts in the middle of the screen have no wheel.
The Measure area panel lay over the vertical dock and showed through other windows.
Search in Tools: the group headings collapsed to the top — while searching they're gone, only tiles remain.
The control points, align north, job package and double measurement windows are full-screen like the others (the HUD used to show through them).
The status pill has shorter texts and a cross with a bigger target; the error log has 2×2 buttons.
Write to the author: the Contact field was unstyled.

verze.nadpis: Pro on request, locked tools at the bottom, compass by the sensor
body: The Pro version isn't bought, it's requested: a full-screen Pro card, the Request Pro button (name, contact, message) — the owner switches it on. Whoever has a key copies it in there.
Locked tools are at the very bottom of Tools in one "In the Pro version" section; the groups at the top are only from what's free.
The tool wheel has the same number of petals for every group (empty ones dashed), Back is exactly at the bottom.
Switch company already on the start screen when the device knows several companies.
The compass reported "silent" even while the map was turning — the watch is now driven by real sensor events.

verze.nadpis: The app is called QTRIG; Basic free, the rest in Pro
body: New name QTRIG and a new icon (Q as a survey target). Address, data and jobs don't change.

Basic free = 21 field actions: measure, area, tie distances, precise GPS, stake out by list, field book, defects, bin, compass, north, GNSS, weather, cadastre where I stand, control points, transfers, change job, handbook, calculator. Axis, polar point, geo-photo, project import, briefing and gestures are in Pro.
Layers: Map/Orthophoto and rotation are free; cadastre, On me, Measure area, Save offline and Show target are in Pro.
Crosses close windows again (a regression from 8 Sep).
The app owner signs in with the name VLASTNIK and password = the key; one icon, everything unlocked.

verze.nadpis: The compass works again, Tools are tidy, the start is snappier
body: The compass stopped asking at the wrong moment. The app requested motion and orientation access right at launch — but an iPhone doesn't allow such a request and answers "denied" even though nobody asked you. That produced the "Compass has no permission" window and a dead arrow in navigation until the end of the session. Now the app asks only on the first touch and after a denial tries once more.

Tools are sorted. Over sixty tiles lay in one heap under the heading "Field tools". Now they're in ten groups by what you do with them — Measure, Determine a new point, Stake out, Record, Align AR, Find out conditions, Cadastre and bases, Before leaving, Company and paperwork, Handbook. And Write to the author stands fixed right at the top, above the search.

Distant points into AR. A new tool (Align AR → Distant points into AR): drag a rectangle in the map with your finger and the points inside show in AR even beyond the set range — e.g. a base two kilometres away. The selection survives closing the app.

Hold a finger on the map = distance from you. A line stretches from your position to the finger and shows the distance. It complements the two-finger measurement, which measures between two places in the map.

Updates without a button. The app takes a new version by itself at launch — just close it and open again. The bar at the top only announces now, nothing is tapped on it. And the backup reminder stopped popping up over the app: it moved to Settings → Maintenance.

Snappier start. Downloading points from ČÚZK compared every downloaded element with all points in the job — with a thousand points that was over two and a half million comparisons and it showed in the app for the first few seconds. On top of that, 56 kB less code is downloaded before the first frame.

Controls: the closing swipe in the Layers window no longer leaves the panel hanging pushed aside, crosses have an honest touch target (and grow in gloves mode) and a swipe over a window's content no longer accidentally launches another tool's shortcut.
In the map only the distance stayed at the navigated point — degrees are gone, the direction is visible from the line itself.

verze.nadpis: Simple mode: the app behind two buttons
body: Switch it on in Settings → Appearance → Controls. The map, camera, dock and tools disappear and only two big buttons remain on screen: Add point and Navigate to point. It's for a day when you only need to mark a spot and walk back — or when you lend the app to someone. The Full app link at the top right leads back to the full app.

Add point = a name (it suggests the next number in the series itself) and one of two buttons: From GPS — averages six seconds on the spot and shows the sample spread — or Manually for Y and X in S-JTSK. Then just Save. The point is saved to the job exactly as from the full app, including where it came from.

Navigate to point shows the job points from the nearest to the farthest. After a tap there's a full-screen arrow and a big distance — nothing more. When the phone doesn't report a heading, the arrow doesn't make it up: it tells you the azimuth as a number.
Saves battery: with the mode on, the camera switches off and the map doesn't redraw. When you switch it off, the app returns exactly to the view it was in.

verze.nadpis: Faster start: the app no longer builds what isn't visible while starting up
body: Points in the map are drawn in batches, nearest first. With a job of a thousand points, nine hundred markers used to be built at once on every start and the phone stood still meanwhile. Now the surroundings where you stand appear at once and the rest fills in when the browser has a quiet moment — blocking at start dropped by half (measured 1,952 → 910 ms).

The Tools window is assembled only after the first touch. The list of actions and the tile grid used to be built right at start-up although nobody looked at them; it cost 0.5 s. Getting to Tools always takes one more tap, so they're ready before you get there — and whoever doesn't touch the app gets them anyway.

Deferred modules no longer get in the way of the first frame. A queue of 2.3 MB of further code was released 0.7 s after page load, i.e. exactly into the last metres of the start. Now it waits longer; whoever starts using the app right away forces it anyway.

verze.nadpis: More at hand: "More" under the tabs, a report with context and a transformation of empty Tools
body: "More" is finally visible. Tutorial and tour, Save for offline, About, History, Share QR and Newsletter hung behind Settings → maintenance → the second-to-last button. Now they stand in a strip right under the Settings tabs, next to Write to the author — from every tab and without scrolling.

A message to the author can attach what the app was just doing. A new checkbox sends the open window, last tool, number of points, job, signal and GPS state and the last three errors from the Error log. Without it, "it doesn't work for me" couldn't be traced; it can be unticked.

Reporting from the Error log takes one tap. The Send to the app author button opens a message pre-filled with the error dump and circumstances — just add what was happening. Sharing and copying the whole log remains.
Empty Tools are no longer mute. In limited mode (without sign-in), instead of an empty grid a card shows what the app can do now, what will come after signing in — and a Sign in button.

verze.nadpis: Write to the author now takes two taps — and works without sign-in too
body: The row "Something's off or missing? Write to the author" is now in Settings right under the search and in the Tools footer. Until now the only path led through Settings → Maintenance → the last button, and whoever isn't signed in couldn't reach it at all — even though they may send a message.
A gesture shortcut. In Gestures and shortcuts there's a new action Write to the author, so an error can be reported in gloves with one stroke, not two windows.
A uniform name. Everywhere it now says Write to the author instead of "Write to me" — with an app you get via a link, "me" doesn't say who you're writing to.

verze.nadpis: Axis stake-out: a polyline axis with chainage and stakes by metres
body: The axis can be a polyline, not only a straight line A→B. Points are entered into the tool (formerly "Line stake-out", now Axis stake-out) in order from the start and the Add vertex button adds as many as needed. Chainage runs across vertices — the second segment continues where the first ended, not from zero.

The read-out finds the segment you stand on by itself. Besides chainage and perpendicular offset the window says which segment you're on (and between which points), how much is left to the vertex and to the end of the axis. You see the same in the collapsed strip and in the camera — the numbers never disagree.

Start chainage aligns the numbers with the design. When the section starts at km 1.200, enter 1200 and the app counts 1200…1400 instead of 0…200 — and the point to stake out is entered directly in design chainage.

Stake out the whole axis by metres. A new command drops stakes into the job at a regular step (every 10, 25, 50 m) along the whole section including its end, optionally offset from the axis. They're named by chainage (ST1225), so the stake-out checklist ticks them off directly.

Vertices are drawn in the camera too. The axis in AR follows the polyline (the corner isn't cut off), vertices have their own rings and the foot of the perpendicular reports the chainage including the start offset.

verze.nadpis: After the overall app walk-through: a manual position from the map is no longer a measurement, the bin restores the whole job
body: A manual position from the map doesn't pretend to be a measured point. When you tapped your position into the map, it leaked into GPS averaging and was saved as if a satellite had measured it. Now a manually entered position is separate and isn't saved as a measurement.
The bin keeps all the job's data. Deleting a job used to sweep away data families the bin couldn't restore. Now the whole job goes into the bin.
Module deferral works again. The app was supposed to load heavy tools only when you open them — but they all got fetched right after start anyway. The start is again what it was meant to be.
File sharing goes one single way. Export, report and backup all end in the same system share sheet, not in ten workarounds depending on the tool.

verze.nadpis: From field reports: the tool wheel no longer shows the same thing twice and the owner's console comes back
body: In the tool wheel ("the flower") a merged tool appears ONCE. Until now there was the Company signpost and right next to it still Attendance, Chat, Walkie-talkie and Accounts separately — the same thing twice. The wheel took the list by a side path that didn't know about the merging. Now the same rule holds everywhere: in the list of actions, in the grid and in the wheel a signpost is one item that opens. Search still finds the individual tools.

The owner's console comes back by itself after closing a tool. Whoever opened something from it lost it — after closing that window an empty map remained and the only way to the next view was a long press on the logo and the key. Now the console reopens where you left off.

The background company check no longer throws anyone out of measuring. Once a minute the app asks the server for the company settings; when that request failed (outage, older token), it sent the surveyor to the sign-in screen in the middle of work. Now such a response is only recorded and the company panel writes about it — nobody is thrown out of the app.

When company administration fails, the app says why. Deleting and editing accounts only showed "Deletion failed". Now you can tell that the server runs an older version that doesn't know that action yet (and that the account can be Blocked instead), as well as that the phone is no longer signed in as company admin.

The Garmin watch guide described the pairing the wrong way round. It promised a "Generate code" button and copying into Garmin Connect — but today the watch shows the code and it's copied into the app. Now the guide fits and it gained a Prepare for the watch part (map and points before leaving).

verze.nadpis: App walk-through: the bin no longer swallows half the deleted points and search doesn't show what the admin forbade
body: The bin handles bulk deletion too. When you deleted several points at once in the Points panel, the app promised "They can be restored from the bin for 30 days" — but the bin only held the last 15 and the rest vanished for good. With bulk deletion "Undo" is deliberately not shown, so the bin is the only rescue there. Now a whole day of work fits in it (400 records) and space is watched by size, not count.

Search no longer reveals tools the role doesn't have. For an employee whose admin forbade a category, the forbidden tiles lit up for two seconds while typing into the search and then went out again. Tapping launched nothing, but the app showed what it shouldn't.

A tool is found under the name the app itself shows. A tile and the row in the list of actions can be named differently ("Voice notes" × "A voice note") and search only used the tile name. Whoever searched for what they read in the app found nothing — and for hidden tools search is the only path to them.

A blocked account really signs out within a minute. When blocking, the admin reads that the account will be signed out on the phone where it's currently signed in too. So far that only held after an app restart — the blocked person still had measuring open. Now the company settings are synced once a minute (in the background and offline nothing happens).

verze.nadpis: Sign-in and company without dead ends, a shorter tool list, full-screen Look around
body: There's a way back from limited mode. Whoever started the app without signing in stayed locked in it — the word "sign in" was nowhere on screen. Now a strip Limited mode — Sign in shows at the bottom above the bar, taking you to the sign-in screen any time.

Everyone can switch company, not just the admin. The company panel gained a Companies section: a list of companies you've ever signed in to, switching (always against the password) and + Join another company (code). The green strip at the top always has the Sign in / switch button — before it showed only to whoever already had a second company.

The "Server unavailable" message stopped lying. In three cases out of four the server was running and only this phone's access was missing. Now it distinguishes no signal, phone not signed in to the server, access expired and server error — and each message has a button that solves it. An empty Attendance also says whether it's empty because nobody clocked in or because the data didn't download.

The tool list shrank by a quarter (80 rows to 59). Related things are now represented by one row that opens: My numbers, Day record, Company, Bases and cadastre, Transfers and devices — alongside the earlier signposts. Nothing disappeared, it just stopped being listed one by one.
Utility networks and Voice note are gone from the menu. They stay in the app and you find them via search, they just no longer take up space among the tools you use.

The "Single determination — unverified" strip disappeared from the point card. It lit under almost every point and scolding a point saved a minute ago for lacking a second determination makes no sense. The deviation and verdict stay where you ask for them yourself — in the Point verification tool.

Look around runs full-screen and gained an Around you list (neighbouring parcels and how far they are). The Show in camera button collapses the window into a pill at the bottom edge so the image is visible; in the camera the boundaries are laid on the ground (terrain is accounted for) and the lines are finally visible in sunlight too.
Windows no longer flicker when opening. The content shows once it's ready — until now the window rendered before the rest was poured in and everything in it jumped.

Dismiss the "Weak GPS" warning with one tap — and it stays dismissed. The cross is now right in the status bubble (before, the path led through the detail and the notification card, i.e. three taps). And above all: dismissing is no longer cancelled by a single tick of good signal. Accuracy in the field jumps around 10 m (9 → 12 → 9 m), so after "OK" the warning kept coming back within seconds; now it's forgotten only after three minutes of continuous good signal — or at once when the signal gets significantly worse, because that's a new situation.
The status bubble is a bit bigger. After slimming it was too thin; two letters of height were added while it still keeps the text on one line.

verze.nadpis: A slim status bubble, full-screen Yearbook, updates once a day, faster gestures and a tool opens even on a quick tap
body: A tool opens even if you tap the tile right after start. The app fetches some tools only after launch so it boots quickly. Whoever was faster than it tapped into nothing — outwardly nothing happened and the tool looked broken. Now such a tap is held and the tool opens by itself as soon as it's ready.

The "New version" bar no longer nags at every launch. It shows at most once a day. You can update manually any time: More → Update history, at the top is a green Update button — and while a new version waits, a badge glows at that item.

The status bubble is a slim pill again. It had doubled because the message wrapped onto two lines. Now the text is rather shortened with an ellipsis and the numbers — accuracy and azimuth — stay in place.

Yearbook and "Points on top of each other" opened INSTEAD of the map. In split the window squeezed between the camera and the map as a third strip and the camera kept running above it. Both windows now run full-screen like all the others.

Gestures react sooner. After the activation gesture a shorter stroke suffices for each shortcut arrow (34 px instead of 54) and it needn't be so exactly horizontal or vertical. The tool also launches immediately — until now it waited two tenths of a second just so the indicator could be seen.

In the company it's visible when the list of people didn't download from the server. Before, the old list from the phone's memory was silently shown in such a case — it looked as if the people had vanished. Now the reason is written at the top (no signal / phone not signed in / expired access) and what to do, plus a Load list from server button.

verze.nadpis: Yearbook, trainer, offline vector map, Look around and new looks
body: New Yearbook in Tools: the year and month in numbers — how far you walked and climbed, how many points you measured, how many days you were in the field — and a map of all points you measured in the year, coloured by month. Quiet badges at the bottom for what went well. Everything stays on the phone, nothing is sent anywhere.

Points on top of each other: when two of you work on a job, the app now recognises that you both measured the same point and asks. When you confirm, the second determination is used as a check measurement — your colleague thereby actually verified the point for you. On top of that, a message to the company chat is no longer lost without signal: it's saved and sent by itself. And the app now says for every accuracy where it comes from — whether someone measured it or the phone only thinks so.
Underneath it all the app stopped freezing on big computations — volumes and other heavy computing run aside, so you can keep panning the map meanwhile.

Field trainer — practice stake-out for real. The app scatters points, you go stake them out and it tells you how many centimetres off you were. Outdoors on real GPS, or at home in a room: there only the position is fictional, you walk by holding a button and go where the phone points — compass and camera are real, so you practise exactly what you do outside. Simulated GPS inaccuracy can be switched on too, because a point that fits on the display needn't fit on the ground yet. Nothing from the trainer is saved to the job and the fictional position doesn't get into measurements.

Offline vector map — a base drawn, not downloaded as an image. Pack an extent from the office (no GPS needed) and have it in the field without signal, sharp at every zoom. A town with surroundings comes to a few MB instead of hundreds. The data is from OpenStreetMap — for orientation, not for measuring.

Look around — a mode for looking about, without a job and without measuring. It tells you which parcel you stand on (number, land type, area), how far the boundary is, your altitude and where the Sun is — and in the camera shows parcel labels over their area. When the boundary is closer than the GPS accuracy, it honestly admits it doesn't know which parcel it is.

Poster of the day — the day as one picture to share: the walked track drawn as a line, points as dots, weather and four big numbers. You'll also find it at the bottom of the Day journal. The kilometres walked and metres of climb come from the phone's GPS, so they're approximate.

Two new looks in Settings → Appearance → Colour tint. Blueprint redraws the whole app and map into the form of a survey drawing — light linework on dark blue, dialogs on graph paper. Night is a red palette with no blue at all: in the dark it doesn't ruin your eye adaptation (that half hour before you can see) and the display glows less. The map, markers and camera image are dimmed too.

Night mode can switch on by itself after dusk and step back in the morning — the switch is right under the tint choice. The app computes the times from your position offline (civil twilight) and won't override your own tint choice: if you pick a different one at night, the automation stays quiet until noon.

New tool North by the Sun (Tools → AR and calibration). The phone's compass is a magnetometer and near rebar, rails or cars it easily shows twenty degrees off. All the previous ways of aligning north need a known point in sight — in the middle of a field there's none. This one needs only a visible Sun: aim at it (or along your own shadow, you don't have to look into the Sun), hold three seconds and the app aligns north. Honestly: by hand it comes to ±3–5°, so it's a rescue where there's nothing to orient on, not a substitute for orientation on a point.

New tool Point from two photos (Tools → Measuring). Determines a point you can't reach — a corner behind a fence, a roof, a chimney, the other side of a river. Unlike forward intersection you don't have to aim the cross steadily: at each station you just snap a photo and tap the target in the frozen image, with a finger, at leisure, even in the car. If you mark a known point in the photo too, the compass error cancels from the result; without it the app marks the result as approximate and says why.

New Guess it (Tools → Aids) — three short disciplines where you first guess and only then learn the truth from the sensors: walk a given distance, turn to a given azimuth, estimate the distance to a point. During an attempt the app deliberately doesn't show what you're guessing. Beyond score and streaks it's a working skill: whoever knows what thirty metres look like and where south-west is spots a silly mistake before saving it. You can play it on a walk without a job too.

verze.nadpis: Other languages, an inbox for messages, faster start and point verification
body: The app speaks English, German and Polish. The language is chosen by the phone and switched at the very top of Settings → Appearance; on the sign-in screen there's a ring at the top right for it. Switching is instant, the app doesn't restart. Technical terminology is translated as a surveyor would, not from a dictionary.

New Write to me ("More" or Settings → Maintenance): send the author what doesn't work, what's missing or what you'd change. You needn't be signed in and it works without signal too — the message waits on the phone and leaves by itself once there's a connection.

Nearest known point: official points (trigonometric, densification, levelling) sorted by distance, with direction and compass point. The Anchor button pre-fills the coordinates straight into the GPS shift to a known point — before they had to be copied by hand.

Check measurement: mark a point for verification, in 25 minutes the app calls and you let it be determined a second time. From the difference of both determinations it computes the real accuracy — unlike σ from one occupation it already includes the systematic error. Then you choose whether to keep the original, average, or overwrite.

Pack the job: one button downloads points, map, cadastre, orthophoto and terrain heights around the job's centre — not around where you happen to stand. At last a trip can be prepared from the office.
The quality report has a new Check column with the verified accuracy of the point and an explanation of how to read it.
Small things: a more precise status bubble and accuracy silhouette, improved gestures as tool shortcuts, company chat, update history and weather; the Garmin watch reads QR better.

The app opens faster. Nine tools that usually aren't even opened all day are now fetched only after rendering — the first frame appears about a third earlier and half a second less passes before the app is ready. Nothing is missing: the tools are in place, they just load in the background.

Point verification (a new tool in Record). The spread of a measurement says how calm the measurement was — not whether the point is right. The GPS error in a phone is shifted in the same direction throughout one occupation, so two hundred calm readings can be two hundred readings off. The only real check is a second determination after a gap. The point card now reports "Verified by second determination · Δ 12 cm (limit 39 cm)" or "Single determination — unverified" and the new tool shows the whole job at once.

Stake-out report (a new tool in Stake out). When you tick a point off, the app now also records where you really stood — and makes a design → reality table with ΔY, ΔX, positional deviation and the limit deviation by quality code. It can be printed, saved as PDF or exported to CSV. Rows where the phone had worse accuracy than half the limit are marked inconclusive — a verdict you can't rely on is worse than none.
In Tools you can now tell which tool touches the job's points: such tiles have a strip at the bottom edge. The others only show.
The error log can be sent with one tap together with the circumstances (app version, phone type, network and GPS state, unloaded modules). Coordinates, job names and point names aren't sent.

verze.nadpis: Fix: sign-in got stuck on "too many attempts"
body: Fixed: the app could refuse even the correct password with a message about many attempts, and immediately — without asking the server at all. There were two defects feeding each other.

First: the phone counted absolutely every server response as a wrong password. Even the one that says "too many attempts, wait". So one lock on the server added errors on the phone too, and the locks added up.

Second: the error counter on the phone never decreased and only a successful sign-in cleared it. Whoever got past nine errors got a quarter-hour lock after every further failure from then on — and couldn't reach success, because the app refused even the correct password. It was a trap with no exit.

Now the counter is forgotten after 30 minutes of quiet and only a genuinely refused password counts as a password-guessing attempt. Protection against PIN guessing stays unchanged: five free attempts, then the wait doubles up to 15 minutes.
Whoever got stuck in that trap signs in straight away after the update — the stuck counter is discarded by itself.

verze.nadpis: GPS accuracy silhouette, quality report and faster start
body: A new accuracy silhouette in the top left corner: a figure standing on the ground and around it a circle of how big the position uncertainty is right now. A circle tight at the feet means good, a circle across the whole card "you're somewhere here". The dotted mark is fixed and corresponds to 5 m, so it reads without counting: inside the dotted = measure, outside = wait. Thresholds and colours are the same as in the status bubble. Switch off in Settings → Appearance.

New tool Quality report: for every point you see what it was measured by, the standard error, the spread of readings σ and how many epochs were used. The app computed this before, but only one number of it reached the point — now it's documentable and can be exported as a report (.txt) or table (.csv) for the office. Hand-entered points have no spread and show a dash.

The app starts faster: twenty tools and exports that open only on demand (regulations, newsletter, backups, calibration, DXF/KML/CSV exports) load only after rendering. Before the first frame 277 kB and 20 files less are processed. Nothing disappeared — the first touch on the bar or Tools fetches the rest at once.

Fixed: solid green buttons had white text in dark mode with a contrast of only 3.35 : 1 — unreadable in direct sun. Now 4.82 : 1, and nine other places were fixed the same way (active tabs, segments, the new-version bar).
Fixed: the "Collapse" button didn't appear at all in some windows — insertion failed when the window heading had its own wrapper.

Inside: errors the app deliberately passes over so it doesn't crash in the field are now written to the Error log (over 1,500 places). Before they vanished without trace and a complaint from the field had nothing to hold on to. A CI check was added that watches colours and contrast, so the two earlier light-mode bugs can't quietly return.
